'''Behzod Sodiqovich Yo‘ldoshev''' ([[Russified]] form '''Bekhzod Sodiqovich Yuldoshev'''; 9 May 1945 – 28 August 2024) was an Uzbek physicist, a science organizer, and a public figure. He served as the president of the [[Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan|Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Uzbekistan]] from 2000 to 2005 and again from 2017 onwards. He was an academician of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan (2000) and held a Doctor of Physical and Mathematical Sciences degree. He died on 28 August 2024, at the age of 79.<ref>{{cite news |title=Скончался глава Академии наук Бехзод Юлдашев |url=https://www.gazeta.uz/ru/2024/08/28/behzod-yuldashev/ |access-date=28 August 2024 |publisher=Gazeta |date=28 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=29 August 2024 |title=Академик Бехзод Юлдашев |work=Pravda Vostoka |pages=3 |language=ru |issue=174}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Born on 9 May 1945 in Tashkent, Yoʻldoshev initially worked as a junior researcher at the Institute of Nuclear Physics of the Academy of Sciences of the Uzbek SSR after he graduated from Tashkent State University in 1968. After defending his thesis in 1971, he went on to work as a senior researcher at the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UgIUAQAAMAAJ |title=Herald of the Russian Academy of Sciences|year=2004 }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite encyclopedia |title=Йўлдошев Беҳзод Содиқович |encyclopedia=[[National Encyclopedia of Uzbekistan|Ўзбекистон миллий энциклопедияси]] |date=2002 |publication-place=Tashkent |lang=uz}}</ref><ref name= "Biography1">{{Cite web|url= https://www.ziyouz.com/portal-haqida/xarita/o-zbek-ziyolilari/behzod-yo-ldoshev-1945|title= BEHZOD YO'LDOSHEV (1945)|website= www.ziyouz.com |access-date= 2023-10-16}}</ref><ref name= "Biography2">{{Cite web|url= https://www.academy.uz/ru/page/yuldashev-bexzod-sodiqovich|title= Yuldashev Behzod Sodiqovich|website= academy.uz- Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan |access-date= 2023-10-16}}</ref><ref name= "Biography3">{{Cite web|url= https://nauka-nanrk.kz/ru/inostrannyh.html|title= Национальная академия наук Республики Казахстан|website= nauka-nanrk.kz|access-date= 2023-10-16|archive-date= 13 May 2020|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200513120118/http://nauka-nanrk.kz/ru/inostrannyh.html|url-status= dead}}</ref>

== Career ==
Having defended his thesis for his doctorate of physical and mathematical sciences in 1981, he went on to be head of a laboratory Physicotechnical Institute of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan, holding that post from 1984 to 1990. In June that year, he became the director of the [[:ru:Институт ядерной физики АН Узбекистана|Institute of Nuclear Physics]], where he remained until 2006. Meanwhile, he became a corresponding member of the Academy of Sciences in 1994, and then a full member in 2000. That year, he was made president of the Academy of Sciences, but he was removed from the post on 21 November 2005. Earlier that year on 24 January, he had been appointed a member of the [[Oliy Majlis]] by decree of [[Islam Karimov|Karimov]]. In 2006 he was demoted to laboratory head in the Institute of Nuclear Physics. In the course of his work, he conducted research outside Uzbekistan, becoming a visiting professor at both [[Stanford University]] and the [[University of Washington]] as well as working on projects with [[Fermilab]] and [[TRIUMF]]. In addition, he worked as a consultant for the [[International Atomic Energy Agency|IAEA]] for four years. Eventually, on 10 January 2017, he was elected to be the president of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan again, and in 2022 he was elected as a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences. As of 2022 he has authored over 400 papers, trained 9 doctoral students, and 30 candidates of sciences.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=ЮЛДАШЕВ Бехзод Садыкович |url=https://centrasia.org/person2.php?st=1013880862 |access-date=2022-12-22 |website=centrasia.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=В Российской академии наук - новые члены из Дубны |url=https://dubna.ru/article/2022/06/v-rossiyskoy-akademii-nauk-novye-chleny-iz-dubny |access-date=2022-12-22 |website=dubna.ru |language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kFMoAQAAMAAJ |title=Гулистон |date=1992 |publisher=Pravda |language=tg}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Бехзод Юлдашев: "Альтернативы атомной энергетике нет!" |url=https://kun.uz/ru/25709537 |access-date=2022-12-22 |website=Kun.uz |language=ru}}</ref><ref name= "Biography1" /><ref name= "Biography2" /><ref name= "Biography3" />

== Scientific works ==
The author of over 300 scientific works, including 3 monographs and 20 inventions, has supervised the research of 9 doctoral candidates and more than 30 candidates for scientific degrees.<ref name= "Biography2" /> He experimentally proved for the first time the existence of a unified mechanism of quark hadronization in interactions between [[neutrino]]s (leptons) and high-energy hadrons with nuclei. He was the first to obtain and interpret experimental evidence for the existence of a new type of hadronic matter - narrow dibaryon resonances ([[dibaryon]]). He discovered the presence of local properties within nuclear matter.<ref>{{Cite web|url= http://www.inp.uz/?q=node%2F305|title= Bekhzad Sadykovich Yuldashev|website= www.inp.uz|access-date= 2023-10-16|archive-date= 4 March 2016|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160304221527/http://www.inp.uz/?q=node%2F305|url-status= dead}}</ref>
